The wastewater treatment process consists of screening, grit removal, seven sequencing batch reactors (activated sludge/secondary clarification), flow equalization, rapid mix/flocculation, filtration, chlorination and dechlorination.
The wastewater treatment process consists of ... filtration, chlorination and dechlorination.
Waste activated sludge is conveyed to three aerobic digesters and dewatered prior to disposal.
Digested sludge is dewatered with a centrifuge and the sludge cake (Class B Biosolids) is delivered directly to a local composting facility.
The Facility can also utilize on-site lined drying beds as a secondary method of dewatering.
Filtrate from the dewatering process is returned to the headworks of the treatment facility.
Undisinfected secondary treated wastewater may be discharged to an unlined storage/percolation basin located in the northwest portion of the Facility.
